newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PX50 CLOSES LOWER AS BEARISH MOOD DEEPENS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PX50 CLOSES LOWER AS BEARISH MOOD DEEPENS.

text.p: Czech shares took another beating on Monday as the sustained downtrend of the last two to three weeks showed no sign of coming to an end and foreign investors continued to stay on the sidelines.
The PX50 index fell five points, 0.9 percent, to 558.4 with dealers predicting that the market could easily go lower as the week progresses.
"It is a mystery to judge when the market will hit bottom," said Petr Opocensky of Citicorp Securities.
"The Czech Republic is looking very weak," added Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka.
Some local analysts also warned that a monthly emerging markets report published on Monday by Robert Fleming & Co could add further momentum to the PX50's descent.
Flemings said that investors should be underweight on the Czech market because of concerns about macroeconomic problems.
One local dealer who did not wish to be named commenting on another bank's report said: "This could really hit the market."
Most major issues again bore the brunt of Monday's decline.
SPT Telecom closed down 54 crowns, 1.5 percent, to 3,440.
